rv.q: Jones’s characters feel so real because she approaches them all with deep and sincere empathy.
Jones raises so many questions and delivers so many truths that the message becomes murky.

Her vividly populated solo show, although often droll, spends much of its 100 minutes presenting precisely the kind of stories that the Trump administration is currently trying to erase from the Smithsonian Institution, and everywhere else.
If you are as yet unaware of the talents of this writer/actress/activist, you owe it to yourself to take a trip to Brooklyn and revel in her presence.

cn.t: Sarah Jones delivers an extraordinary one-woman showcase, cycling through nearly twenty vividly drawn characters with distinct accents and backgrounds to explore America's relationship with trauma and politics in this compelling return to form.
